主要内容: Starbucks reported fourth-quarter revenue that missed analysts' expectations, leading to a selloff after the market closed. The company's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue was $5.7 billion, below the $5.80 billion projected by Thomson Reuters. Same-store sales in the U.S. rose 2 percent, falling short of the 3.3 percent growth anticipated by analysts. Starbucks revised its long-term guidance for EPS growth to at least 12 percent, down from the previous target of 15 to 20 percent. The company attributed its performance to slowing foot traffic at malls and changing dining habits, as well as the impact of severe hurricanes in the U.S. Global comparable-store sales rose 2 percent, with a 3 percent increase excluding the impact of Hurricanes Harvey and Irma. Starbucks plans to sell its Tazo tea brand to Unilever for $384 million, with the deal expected to close in the fourth quarter. The company also announced a 20 percent increase in its cash dividend to 30 cents per share and a new co-branded credit card with Chase.
